_comment: One definition of 'a successful access record', consumed by both languages.
The desktop shell decides whether to mirror a backend stdout line into tauri.log,
and the backend decides whether to emit it at all. Those are two implementations of
the same idea in two languages and two processes, so they can drift; the CRLF
handling in the progress-frame collapsers already did drift once.
Python reads this from tests/test_log_rule_parity.py. Rust reads it from the
shared_access_log_fixture_tests module in src-tauri/src/process.rs. A change to the
rule on one side turns the other side red.
keep=false means the line is a successful access record that tauri.log may drop
because it is already on the phase log and the backend session log.

cases.name: plain 200 access record
cases.why: the duplicated line this whole mechanism exists to drop

cases.name: 199 is not success
cases.why: lower edge; anything outside 2xx keeps its line

cases.name: 300 is not success
cases.why: a redirect is not a success and must stay visible

cases.name: 404 failure
cases.why: the line a support engineer is looking for

cases.name: request_completed with no status_code
cases.why: a record we cannot vouch for is kept rather than guessed at

cases.name: status_code is a string
cases.why: not an integer, so the success test does not apply

cases.name: a different structured event
cases.why: only request_completed is an access record

cases.name: malformed JSON
cases.why: unparseable, so it is not recognised as an access record

cases.name: leading whitespace before the object
cases.why: both sides trim the start before parsing
